primitives.meaning: a connection attempt recorded against a named integration by a named configurer; a recorded outcome from the authentication, scope and capability checks
entryFilters: a connection attempt recorded against a named integration by a named configurer
a recorded outcome from the authentication, scope and capability checks
no instance of this journey is already open for the the single connection attempt and the integration it configures
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

primitives.asks: How far did the attempt get?

branches.label: Active
branches.test: authentication, required scope and the capability probe all passed and the connection is recorded active

branches.label: Failed at a named stage
branches.test: the attempt failed and which stage failed is authoritatively recorded

branches.label: Failed, stage unidentified
branches.test: the attempt failed and no stage is authoritatively identified

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

primitives.purpose: Confirm the connection is active and name the capabilities that were actually validated rather than the ones that were configured.
primitives.brief: Confirm the connection is active and name the capabilities that were actually validated rather than the ones that were configured. The difference is what stops somebody building on a permission they do not have
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.reEntry: a further connection to the same provider is a new instance

branches.label: Credential
branches.test: the provider refused the credential or the authorisation was never completed

branches.label: Permission
branches.test: the credential was accepted but a required permission was not granted

branches.label: Capability
branches.test: credential and permission both passed but the safe probe could not perform the minimum operation

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

primitives.purpose: Say the credential itself was refused and give the one step that re-establishes it.
primitives.brief: Say the credential itself was refused and give the one step that re-establishes it. This is the only stage the configurer can usually fix unaided, and it is the one most often buried under a generic error
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

primitives.purpose: Name the specific permission that is missing and where it is granted.
primitives.brief: Name the specific permission that is missing and where it is granted. A missing permission reported as a failed setup makes somebody redo an entire connection to change one switch
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

primitives.purpose: Say that access was granted but the minimum operation could not be performed, and name which operation.
primitives.brief: Say that access was granted but the minimum operation could not be performed, and name which operation. This usually sits with a limit on the provider side, so the message points there rather than at the configurer

mustNotClaim: that a saved credential is a connection

primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

primitives.purpose: Say the attempt failed, that the stage has not been identified, and that nothing further is needed from the configurer while it is looked at.
primitives.brief: Say the attempt failed, that the stage has not been identified, and that nothing further is needed from the configurer while it is looked at. Admitting there is no cause yet beats inventing one - a guessed cause sends somebody to fix what is not broken
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.on: a failed connection attempt with no stage authoritatively identified
carries: the attempt, its provider and what the configurer has already been told
which stages did pass before the failure

cancelOn.meaning: a further connection attempt is recorded

primitives.reads: the the single connection attempt and the integration it configures re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

primitives.asks: What did the next attempt do?

branches.label: Now active
branches.test: a later attempt passed every stage and the connection is recorded active

branches.label: Failed again
branches.test: a later attempt failed at a stage that has already been named to the configurer

branches.label: Failed at a different stage
branches.test: a later attempt cleared the stage that was named and failed at one that has not been named yet

branches.label: Removed
branches.test: the configuration was removed before any attempt succeeded

primitives.state: still not connected after the named fix
primitives.reEntry: a later attempt re-enters at the outcome check; a fix already given is not sent twice

primitives.state: abandoned before the connection was ever made
primitives.reEntry: a new attempt on the same integration starts a fresh instance
